texts.facts: 1. The present complaint is filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 10.07.2008 at about 6:18 PM Food Inspector Gian Chand purchased a sample of 'SAUNF LAL MIX DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. (FRESHNER)' an article of food for analysis from accused No. 1 Sushil Yadav of M/s V-Mart Retail. Ltd. (formerly known as V-Mart Retail Pvt. Ltd) 370 Kohat Enclave, Main Road, Pitampura, Delhi- 110034 where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No. 1 Sushil Yadav was found vending the article of food at the time of taking the sample. The sample consisted of 9 sealed polypacks of 100 gm each having identical label declaration as reproduced on Form VI. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh.B.S.Thakur, SDM/LHA. Food Inspector divided the sample of the article of food into three equal parts by taking three polypacks together as one sample counterpart. Each counter part containing the sample was separately packed. fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act, 1954 & Rules, 1955. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the sample counterpart containing the sample. Notice in Form VI was given to accused No.1 Sushil Yadav and the price of sample was also paid to him vide vendor receipt dated 10.07.2008. Vendor also issued cash memo. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. Notice in form VI was also prepared for Abhi Enterprises, WZ-1358, Second floor, Nangal Rai, Delhi-110084, the alleged supplier. All the documents prepared by me were signed by accused No. 1 Sushil Yadav and by the Da vs Sushil Yadav Etc. on 14 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165018929/ 2 other witness Sh.S.N.Jindal, FA. Before taking the sample efforts were made to get the public witnesses to join the proceedings but none came forward, as such Sh.S.N.Jindal, FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code Number 61/LHA/22526 in intact condition along with copy of memo in DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. Form VII and another copy of memo in Form VII under seal cover were sent separately to the Public Analyst, Delhi on 11.07.2008 and two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of memos in Form VII were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact conditions on 11.07.2008. All copies of Memos in Form VII bear the seal impression with which sample parts were sealed. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be adulterated and misbranded. The report of Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample is Adulterated because total dye content of synthetic colour used exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 100 ppm. The sample is also Misbranded because there is violation of Rule-24 and 32b and Rule-36(2)(a)and Rule-42 "ZZZ(1)." The public analyst has also reported in the above said report regarding label Without declaration of extraneous addition of synthetic colour artificial sweetener and ingredients size of label is only 16% of the size of packet." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Sushil Yadav was the Vendor-cum Assistant Store Manager of M/s V-Mart Retail Ltd (formerly known as V Mart Retell Pvt Ltd), 370 Kohet Enclave, Main Road, Pitampura, Delhi110034 at the time of taking sample and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. Letters dt 08.08.2008, 19.11.2008, 22.12.2008 were sent to vendor and letters dt 28.08.2008, 15.09.2008, 13.10.2008, 04.11.2008 were sent by food inspector to Registered Office of the company asking for the Constitution of the company and the Directors ln-charge and responsible for day today conduct of the business of the DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. company but no reply was furnished by the company deliberately though they were also informed about the information received from Registrar of Companies regarding the list of directors of company. Accused No. 5 M/s V-Mart Retail Pvt. Ltd having Regd. office at F-15 Udyog Nagar lndl Area, Rohtak Road, Peeragarhi, New Delhi-110049 is a company and as per office of Registrar of Companies the company has three Directors i.e accused No. 2 La|it Aggarwal, accused No.3 Hemant Madan Gopal Aggarwal, accused No. 4 Madan Gopal Aggarwal and in absence of nomination, all three Directors are incharge & responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the company. Being a company M/s V-Mart Retail Ltd. is also liable. 5. It is further stated that the vendor/accused No.1 Sushil Yadav disclosed that the sampled article of food "Saunf Lal Mix (Freshner)" was supplied to them by M/s Abhi Enterprises WZ- 1358, IInd Floor, Nangal Rai, Delhi-84 but no documentary evidence was produced by him. During the course of investigation, it was found that M/s Abhi Enterprises is non- existent and is a fictitious firm. The vendor as well as directors of the company did not disclose to me the true name, address and other particulars of the person from whom they had purchased the article of food. 6. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 12.10.2009 alleging violation of Da vs Sushil Yadav Etc. on 14 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165018929/ 3 Section 2(ia)(a)(j)&(m), 2(ix)(h),(k) of the PFA Act, 1954, and the provision of Rule 24,30 & 32(b), 36(2)(a), 42(ZZZ) DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. (1) of PFA Rules 1955, as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act by the accused person. 7. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 12.10.2009. The accused thereafter exercised his option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL and pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) and 16(1A) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(j)&(m), 2(ix)(h),(k) of the PFA Act, 1954 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. During the trial, the accused No. 1 was declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 26.10.2010. 8. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sh Gian Chand, PW-2 SDM/LHA B.S. Thakur, and PW-3 FA S.N. Jindal. PW-1 and PW-3 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh B.S. Thakur. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting of nine sealed poly packs 100 gms each of Saunf Lal Mix (Freshner) bearing label declaration, dividing the sample equally in three counterparts by putting three sealed poly packs as one counterpart, each counterpart was packed, fastened, marked and sealed and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B, notice u/s 14A Ex.PW1/C, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/D. Raid Report under Rule 9(e) Ex.PW1/E was prepared at the spot. Thereafter, on the next working day i.e. 11.08.2008, one counterpart alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VII in a separate sealed cover were deposited with PA vide PA's Receipt Ex.PW1/F and the remaining two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/G under intimation that one counterpart of the sample has already been deposited with the PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/H was received stating that the sample was found adulterated as well as misbranded. Thereafter, on the directions of SDM/LHA, PW-1 started the investigations and received the Notice u/s 14 A with the remark on returned envelope Ex. PW1/I that 'no such firm was there'. The said returned Notice U/s 14 A of the PFA Act Ex. PW 1/I-1. During further investigations, PW-1 sent a Letter to the vendor SushiI Yadav through speed post vide Ex.PW1/J which was also received back undelivered with the remark on returned envelope Ex.PW1/J-1 stating that 'the addressee i.e the vendor / accused refused to accept the same'. Thereafter, PW-1 delivered a copy of the same letter Ex.PW1/J2 by hand to the vendor. Thereafter, PW-1 sent a letter Ex.PW1/K and a reminder Ex. PW1/K-1 to M/s V. Mart Retail Pvt. Ltd. through speed post at their registered office situated at F-15, Udyog Nagar, Industrial Area, Rohtak Road, Peeragarhi, Delhi but no reply of the same was received. Thereafter, PW-1 sent a reminder Ex. PW1/K-2 to M/s V. Mart Retail Pvt. Ltd. at their registered office as well at their DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. place of business asking them to confirm the name of the Directors, which were obtained by me from Ministry of Company Affairs. PW-1 further sent a reminder Ex. PW 1/K-3 to the said Company but no reply of these reminders was received. PW-1 also sent letter Ex. PW1/L to the vendor at his residential office as well at the registered office Da vs Sushil Yadav Etc. on 14 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165018929/ 4 of the Company and reminder vide Ex.PW1/L-1 through registered post. Thereafter PW-1 sent a letter vide Ex.PW1/M to VAT Officer, Ward No. 106 seeking information on the constitution of M/s V. Mart Retail Pvt. Ltd. and received its reply stating that Lalit Aggarwal was the authorized signatory of the said Company. PW-1 obtained information from PFA Department vide his request Ex.PW1/M-1 and received reply stating that 'there was no nominee of M/s V. Mart Retail Pvt. Ltd.. Thereafter, PW-1 sent a letter Ex.PW1/M-2 to the Registrar of Companies asking to disclose the information on the constitution of M/s V. Mart Retail Pvt. Ltd. but the same was received undelivered vide Envelope Ex.PW1/M-3. Thereafter, PW-1 obtained information from the office of Ministry of Companies, Connaught Place, New Delhi vide Ex.PW1/M-4 wherein it was found that on the date of sampling, there were 3 Directors i.e. Shri Lalit Aggarwal, (ii) Shri Hemant Madan Gopal Aggarwal and (iii) Shri Madan Gopal Aggarwal. Thereafter, PW-1 sent a Letter to VAT Officer, Ward No. 60 vide Ex. PW1/N and a letter to Ex. PW1/N-1 to VAT Officer, Ward No. 61 for seeking information on the constitution of M/s Abhi Enterprises and received reply from Ward No. 61 stating that 'M/s Abhi Enterprises was working at RZF-4, Raj Nagar-II, Palam Colony, Delhi and was dealing in Electrical Appliances. Thereafter PW-1 sent letter Ex. PW1/O to M/s Abhi Enterprises, WZ-1358, Ind Floor, Nangal Raya Delhi DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. through registered post but no reply of the same was received. HE also sent letter to M/s Abhi Enterprises, RZF-4, Raj Nagar-Il, Palam Colony, Delhi vide Ex.PW1/O-1 but the same was received back undelivered vide postal envelope Ex.PW1/O-2. Thereafter, on conclusion of investigations, PW-1 sent the entire case file to the then Director PFA, Shri Mohan Lal through concerned SDM/LHA. for obtaining his Consent. The then Director PFA, granted his Consent for prosecution Ex. PW 1/P. Thereafter, on the directions of SDM/LHA, PW-1 filed the complaint Ex.PW1/Q before the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/R alongwith the copy of PA Report was sent to the accused persons through SDM/LHA Shri Pradeep Baijal, which were not received back undelivered. All the witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel. 9. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 17.02.2018 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
texts.arguments: 14. In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned. 15. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. For all purposes the report of the public analyst is replaced by the DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. certificate of the Director.... It means obliterate, [LEAKAGE_MASK], annul, replace, make void, inefficacious or useless, repeal. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed that "According to the scheme of the Act, the Director of Central Food Laboratory is constituted to be a sort of greater expert than the Public Analyst and his certificate supersedes the report of Public Analyst under sub-section (3) of section 13". The Hon'ble Court also took a note of the ruling in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970] wherein it was observed that the right has been given to the vendor for his satisfaction and proper defence, to get the sample analysed by a "greater expert whose certificate is to be accepted by court as conclusive evidence". Reliance can be placed on Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Zahiruddin [ILR (1972) 1 Del 630]. Thus, evidence can be given by the accused to disprove the report of PA, but once the accused exercises his right under DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. section 13(2) of the Act upon which Certificate is given by CFL, such a certificate of CFL would supersede the PA report and would become final and conclusive. The CFL report has been assailed by the defence on the ground that the sample was analysed by CFL after the expiry of the product in question and the defence has relied upon the Da vs Sushil Yadav Etc. on 14 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165018929/ 6 judgement of of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State of Haryana vs Unique Farmaid P. Ltd & Ors 1999 (2) FAC399 to argue that the sample was packed on 06/08 and was best before 11/08. In the words of Hon'ble Court :- "Sub-section (1) of Section 30 which appears to be relevant only DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. prescribes in effect that ignorance would be of no defence but that does not mean that if there are contraventions of other mandatory provisions of the Act, the accused have no remedy. In The State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd., JT (1996) 10 SC 480 this Court in somewhat similar circumstances said that the procedure laid down under Section 24 of the Act deprived the accused to have sample tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory and adduce evidence of the report so given in his defence. In this connection reference be made to decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal & Ors., [1998] 5 DA vs Sushil Yadav etc. SCC 343 under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram, AIR (1967) SC 970; Chetumal v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr., [1981] 3 SCC 72 and Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf & Anr., [1999] 2 SCC 400 all under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Under Da vs Sushil Yadav Etc. on 14 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165018929/ 7 sub-section (3) of Section 24 report signed by the Insecticide analyst shall be evidence of the facts stated therein and shall be conclusive evidence against the accused only if the accused do not, within 28 days of the receipt of the report, notify in writing to the Insecticides Inspector or the Court before which proceedings are pending that they intend to adduce evidence to controvert the report. Therefore, placing reliance upon the aforesaid judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State of Haryana vs Unique Farmaid P. Ltd & Ors, Hindustan Liver Ltd Vs State of Punjab 2011 (1) FAC 192, a benefit of doubt is given to the accused regarding the adulteration of the sample, which is the subject matter of the present case. Reliance may further be had upon the case titled as Food Inspector vs Banarsi Das & Ors 2014 (2) FAC 177 wherein the order of declining cognizance was uphold by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi when the complaint was filed after expiry period of the product more particularly when no preservative was added to the sample as per the prosecution evidence. Reliance may further be had on the judgement of Marico Ltd and others vs State of Delhi 2015 (1) FAC 40. 21. Regarding accused No. 2,3,& 4 who are the directors of accused No. 5 company, it is not proved on record that they were incharge and responsible to the company for the conduct of the business and for this purpose, the defence has relied upon Shyam Sunder Bhatia and Ors vs State through Food Inspector Govt of NCT of Delhi 2009(2)RCR(Criminal) 417.
